chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: Goldkette lets the band go; musicians too drunk to find their chairs
summary: Goldkette handled bookings and let the band do as it liked; Morehouse recalls players feeling for their chairs yet playing like mad.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Really. What did Jean Goldkette was a businessman. How did he feel about all these people cutting up?
He didn't know what to do with them. He didn't know the first thing what to do with them.
Yeah. He let them do what they wanted to do.
So he took care of I guess the booking and whatever was there. Because my brother Charlie was right in there trying to make the fellows play, and behave
themselves. And he go up and drag them out. And they were not dressed half the time.
Really. They didn't have the.. .. to wear a bow tie.
Sure, they used to go around feeling for the chairs.
This wasn't all the time.There were many bad times.
You mean they couldn't walk without holding on to the chairs.
And this is when they went to play for a dance?
There wasn't anything wrong with their playing.
